title: رقم يتجاوز الألف.. القصة المؤلمة وراء إصابات مانويل نوير
summary: 1222 يومًا من الغياب
body: 1222 يومًا من الغياب تلقى بايرن ميونخ ضربة جديدة ومؤلمة بإصابة قائده وحارسه المخضرم مانويل نوير، لتتجدد معاناة صاحب الـ40 عامًا مع الإصابات، بعدما تحولت مسيرته في السنوات الأخيرة إلى سلسلة طويلة من فترات الغياب التي أثرت على انتظام مشاركاته مع الفريق البافاري. وذكرت صحيفة "بيلد" الألمانية أن نوير تعرض لتمزق جزئي في أحد أوتار القدم اليمنى، خلال مواجهة ماينز التي انتهت بفوز بايرن ميونخ بنتيجة (2-1)، يوم السبت، ضمن منافسات الدوري الألماني. وبحسب معلومات الصحيفة، فإن الحارس الألماني سيغيب عن الملاعب لمدة تصل إلى شهرين، في ضربة جديدة للفريق الذي سيفتقد خدمات قائده خلال الفترة المقبلة. وكشفت بيلد عن حجم المعاناة التي عاشها نوير بسبب الإصابات، مشيرة إلى أن فترات غيابه السابقة، قبل الإصابة الأخيرة، وصلت إلى 1222 يومًا، في رقم يعكس حجم المتاعب البدنية التي طاردت الحارس المخضرم طوال مسيرته، ويضيف فصلًا جديدًا إلى سجله الطبي المليء بالإصابات. ناقش الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديات كووورة

Concrete monolithic buildings loom along every major road, with names like Skybox and CloudHQ. It’s accepted wisdom in Big Tech that the war against data centers must be about something bigger than just data centers themselves. title: رسميا.. مبابي يهزم يامال ويخطف جائزة مرموقة
summary: المنافسة مستمرة بين النجمين
body: المنافسة مستمرة بين النجمين حسم كيليان مبابي، نجم ريال مدريد، المنافسة الفردية التي جمعته بلامين يامال، جناح برشلونة، بعدما تُوج بجائزة أفضل لاعب في الدوري الإسباني عن شهر أكتوبر، ليحصد أول انتصار مباشر بينهما على مستوى الجوائز الفردية منذ خسارتهما سباق الكرة الذهبية لعام 2026 أمام هاري كين. وجاء فوز المهاجم الفرنسي بعد منافسة ضمت خمسة لاعبين، تقدمهم يامال، إلى جانب جونكالو جيديش لاعب ريال سوسيداد، وأليخاندرو جريمالدو لاعب أتلتيكو مدريد، وماتياس ديتورو حارس مرمى إلتشي. ناقش الموضوعات والأخبار بشكل أعمق في منتديات كووورة أرقام مبابي تحسم المنافسة استند تتويج مبابي إلى حصيلته التهديفية المميزة خلال أكتوبر، بعدما سجل أربعة أهداف في ثلاث مباريات بالدوري الإسباني، ليؤكد تأثيره الكبير في نتائج ريال مدريد خلال الشهر. وكانت أبرز محطاته تسجيل ثنائية أمام إشبيلية، قبل أن يكرر الإنجاز بهدفين في شباك برشلونة خلال مواجهة الكلاسيكو، التي انتهت بفوز الفريق الملكي بنتيجة 2-1 على ملعب سبوتيفاي كامب نو. وبفضل هذه الأهداف، رفع مبابي رصيده إلى 11 هدفًا في الدوري الإسباني، إضافة إلى تمريرتين حاسمتين، ليصل إجمالي مساهماته التهديفية إلى 13، مع ختام مباريات أكتوبر. body: Archaeologists excavating in northeastern France have unearthed a small fifth-century cemetery containing the graves of two Germanic chieftains and two warhorses. The burial ground is providing new information about the transitional period after the fall of the Roman Empire . The burial complex was discovered near the city of Colmar, just a few miles from the Rhine River, which forms the border between France and Germany. This area had a Gallo-Roman village from the first to the third centuries, and archaeologists found several ancient houses, hearths, wells and craft areas, according to a Nov. 6 translated statement from the French National Institute for Preventive Archaeological Research (Inrap). Archaeologists also uncovered a rare fifth-century cemetery at the site, which was used from about A.D. 450 to 500, a critical time period in Western Europe because of the collapse of the Roman Empire . title: NASA's destroyed Swift Observatory took one of the best-ever photos of bright Andromeda
summary: NASA's Swift Observatory went out in a blaze of glory this week, but it left behind millions of images of the universe that could fuel discoveries for decades.
body: Early Wednesday (Nov. 4), NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory fell out of space, burning up in the sky over Sumatra . It was a fitting, fiery end for a telescope that spent 22 years studying the most powerful explosions in the universe — and, even with Swift gone, its observations will continue to feed scientific curiosity for years to come. Swift's most important contributions to astronomy are not exactly eye candy. Designed to swivel toward deep-space explosions at a moment's notice, Swift excelled at capturing bright, fleeting and faraway specks of light. The multiwavelength observatory was equipped with optical, ultraviolet (UV) and X-ray instruments, allowing it to catch cosmic bursts of energy across the electromagnetic spectrum, zeroing in on flares of light that other telescopes might miss. One of its most significant detections was a gamma-ray burst — an incredibly bright blast, likely emitted by a giant star as it exploded in a supernova before collapsing into a black hole. body: A peanut allergy diagnosis in infancy can mean years of avoiding the food or undergoing treatments to build tolerance. In an analysis published in The Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology: In Practice , researchers conducted supervised "food challenges" with infants diagnosed with a peanut allergy. These challenges involved giving the babies increasing amounts of peanut protein, with the intention of confirming whether they indeed had an allergy. title: Physicists sank a telescope 1.5 miles under the sea to put Einstein's relativity to the test
summary: A half-built neutrino telescope on the floor of the Mediterranean Sea searched for cracks in one of physics' most basic invariances. It came up empty, but its limits rival those of detectors many times its size.

(Image credit: Edward Berbee/Nikhef) A particle-detecting telescope sunk more than a mile beneath the sea off the coast of France has tested a core principle of Einstein's relativity and found no cracks. The detector, called Oscillation Research with Cosmics in the Abyss (ORCA) , detects elusive particles called neutrinos. As a doctoral student, Alba Domi rode onto the Mediterranean aboard one of two boats that helped build the telescope, lowering some of its first detection units to the seafloor about 1.5 miles (2.4 kilometers) below the waves off Toulon, France. Now, data from those first detection units have been used to test one of the founding rules of Einstein’s relativity: the idea that the laws of nature look the same no matter which way you face or how fast you move. The team found no sign that this rule, called Lorentz invariance, is broken. summary: An analysis of plant fossils preserved in amber from Myanmar revealed that the West Burma Block, a chunk of crust that broke off of Australia, seeded Southeast Asia's lush tropical forests.
body: Southeast Asia's tropical forests owe their rich biodiversity to a tiny fragment of Earth's crust that split from what is now northwestern Australia roughly 150 million years ago, a new study reports. The fragment transported hundreds of flowering species and a flourishing collection of other ancient plants north across the prehistoric Tethys Ocean, the research reveals. The findings contradict previous theories that the fragment originated closer to what is now Southeast Asia and that Southeast Asia's tropical forests evolved sometime after the extinction of the dinosaurs around 66 million years ago. At the time the fragment formed, Australia was connected to Antarctica and India within the ancient supercontinent Gondwana, which the Tethys Ocean separated from another ancient supercontinent, called Laurasia. After drifting northward for 100 million years, the microplate eventually collided with Southeast Asia, seeding tropical forests that evolved into the lush ecosystems found in this part of the world today, the researchers said. body: A noxious gas found seeping through cracks on Mars hints that there may be magma flowing beneath the Red Planet's surface — and perhaps even an environment similar to habitable ones on Earth, a new study suggests. Europe's ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter (TGO) spacecraft spotted a possible signal of hydrogen chloride gas leaking from rifts in the region of Alba Mons, the largest volcano on Mars in terms of surface area. (Mars' famous Olympus Mons is the largest volcano in terms of height.) Scientists interpret this gas as emissions from hot magma below the regolith of Mars. Although more research is required to confirm the emissions, the team suggested that Alba Mons may host an environment similar to hydrothermal vents on Earth, where life once likely arose and continues to thrive today. title: Southern Taurid meteor shower could bring fireballs ‪this week —‬ when and where to look
summary: The best time to see meteors during the Southern Taurid meteor shower is coming up soon.
body: One of autumn's best opportunities to see brilliant "fireballs" arrives overnight Wednesday and Thursday (Nov. 4-5) during the Southern Taurid meteor shower. Although the Southern Taurids are a minor meteor shower that produces only a handful of "shooting stars" each hour, it occasionally features exceptionally bright meteors called fireballs, which can briefly light up the night sky. According to NASA , fireballs are meteors at least as bright as Venus . The Southern Taurids are active for several weeks in fall and peak Oct. 14, but the American Meteor Society expects the "fireball swarm component" to peak around Nov. 4-5. Meteors can streak across any part of the sky, but for this meteor shower, they appear to radiate from the constellation Taurus, which will rise in the eastern sky as night falls and climb higher as the night progresses. That makes the hours around midnight a good time to look for shooting stars. However, unlike major meteor showers such as the Perseids (which peak Aug. 12-13) and the Geminids (which peak Dec. 13-14), the Southern Taurids have a broad peak, so there's no need to be outside at an exact time. title: When dinosaurs are sold to the highest bidder, we all lose
summary: The sale of the Nanotyrannus "Jodi" for over $47 million shines a stark light on the commodification of Earth's history, say Kristi Curry Rogers and Lindsay Zanno.
body: Dinosaurs are more than extraordinary specimens with massive price tags. They are irreplaceable snapshots of our planet's history and our own human journey. When scientifically important fossils are reduced to luxury commodities, we are robbed of the evidence that makes them valuable in the first place. On Oct. 27, a 19.6-foot-long (6 meters) skeleton of Nanotyrannus lancensis known as "Jodi" was sold at Sotheby's in New York for $47,255,000, far exceeding its $6 million to $9 million estimate. The buyer and seller were not identified. It was the latest in a string of multimillion-dollar dinosaur auctions, following the $50.1 million sale of a T. rex (Gus) in July and the $44.6 million sale of a Stegosaurus (Apex) in 2024. Sea surface temperatures were as high as 82 degrees Fahrenheit (28 degrees Celsius), while at a depth of 330 feet (100 meters) water temperatures ranged from 66 to 67 F (18.9 to 19.4 C) — up to 9 F (5 C) warmer than usual for that time of the year. Around 400,000 years after the Big Bang , the fledgling universe finally cooled enough to form atoms — mostly hydrogen. Then, after the first stars flickered to life and gathered into galaxies, bursts of radiation ionized the neutral hydrogen. This turned the impenetrable fog of atoms into electrically charged protons and electrons, allowing light to pass through interstellar space unimpeded and, eventually, reach our observatories. title: Are sharks really older than trees?
summary: It seems like a simple question, but it needs serious taxonomic sleuthing. Are sharks or trees the oldest?
body: You may have heard that sharks are older than trees. And yes, sharks are truly ancient, with an evolutionary lineage dating back hundreds of millions of years. But are they really older than trees? Experts told Live Science that the answer depends on what we classify as a shark. "It's all in the fine print," John Maisey , the curator-in-charge emeritus of fossil fish at the American Museum of Natural History in New York, told Live Science. "The takeaway is that the shark lineage within the fishes generally does go back further than trees. But it really depends on how you define what we mean by shark." The modern sharks we see today first emerged around 195 million years ago, during the Jurassic period. Fossils of ancient sharks from this time can be traced to living lineages, namely Hexanchiformes , an order of sharks identified by their six or seven gills and single dorsal fin. This means that modern sharks, at least, are not older than trees. Experts generally agree that trees first evolved in the Middle Devonian epoch, around 380 million to 390 million years ago. But a new study suggests that the outer giants may develop weirdly shaped orbits as the sun runs out of fuel, causing the planets to cross paths and destroy themselves through collisions within three billion years of the sun's transformation into a red giant.
